title: Tables
story: Tables are for data in rows and columns. Headers use <th>, cells use <td>.
goal: Build a table with a header row (Item, Price) and 2 rows of data.
starter: Shop prices

tests.label: Two header cells: Item and Price
tests.js: var h = $$("th").map(txt); return (h.length === 2 && h[0] === "Item" && h[1] === "Price") || "headers: " + h.join(", ")

tests.label: Two data rows
tests.js: return $$("tbody tr").length === 2 || $$("tbody tr").length + " data rows (put data rows in tbody)"

tests.label: Each data row has 2 cells
tests.js: return $$("tbody tr").every(function (r) { return r.querySelectorAll("td").length === 2; }) || "a row has the wrong number of td cells"

hints: <tr> is a row. Inside it use <th> for headings and <td> for data.
Put the header row in <thead> and the data rows in <tbody>.
socratic: How many cells should every row have?
What is the difference between th and td?
Should you use a table to arrange a page layout?
explain: In one sentence: what did you learn from “Tables”?
